structured_output.summary: Phase 12 (Red Team dataplane qualification and delivery) is substantively complete and its evidence survives adversarial verification. The recorded gate docs/checks/phase-12.json is the full 39-command set defined in tools/check_phase.py:71-113 (I compared the recorded "command" arrays one-for-one), every exit_code is 0, timeout false, source_unchanged true, and source_sha256 is de311207659ad73a8a158b79e262714b24e5c158441ee3d40adbe5b4e5e98bce — independently reproduced by a second artifact (docs/checks/phase-12-private-material.json:4, 1487 git-visible files, 0 credential/registration matches). All thirteen child reports exist and contain real execution: 1.89.0/1.99.0 default/minimal/all plus isolated MSRV red-team (actual rustc 1.89.0/1.99.0 banners, 171/203/145 lib tests and per-integration-binary results), native export consumers (3,820 frozen capabilities, 100s run), packaged archives on both compilers that extract and actually run the new example (phase-12-package-1.89.0.json:818-828), and a clean dependency audit (0 vulnerabilities, 0 license errors, 206 locked deps). Contract completeness is strong: tools/red_team_dataplane.py recounts 47 operations from the pinned YAML (sha256 77f015de… equals the Phase 9 pin), fails on any hash/ID/set drift, binds each operation's request/response schema literals to the individual native method body (verify_schema_binding, red_team_dataplane.py:526-541) with transposed-root negatives, requires a real dispatch arm per fixture, and derives the 12 rejected legacy options from actual public option structs against a pinned reviewed set. All six phase-11 follow-ups are implemented and tested, not merely asserted: per-method schema-root binding, contract-invalid JSON response tests on all ten new typed routes (red_team_contracts.rs:2439-2476), embedded contract.json reduced to queryKinds/querySchema only, exactly 47 dispatch arms with no unreachable frozen-only arms, and the live-attempt naming convention documented at docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:35-38. Security behaviour for new routes is covered concretely (invalid path IDs, cancellation/deadline before and after dispatch, no-replay across transport/http/decode/limit for all six writes, destination re-check before auth, redaction, exact CSV bytes including empty/non-UTF8/over-limit, FileFormat::Unknown("CSV") rejection, 409 preservation, open ReportState). Live acceptance is reported separately and honestly: receipt phase-08-live-attempt-12.json is source-bound (runtimeInputsSha256 equality enforced by live_evidence.py:266) and records red_team probes at HTTP 403 with all eleven new operations live-unverified. Remaining issues are documentation and tooling polish, not correctness: the RED_TEAM.md pagination paragraph was not reconciled with the new pre-auth rejection of skip/limit/search, PLATFORMS.md still points at the older of two retained GNU matrix receipts, and the query-kind lowering has no explicit unsupported-kind guard. Remote push and remote CI are correctly still pending the gate.

findings.description: The pagination section still states "Direct list calls omit unspecified `skip`, `limit`, and `search` fields", which is now inaccurate for the eight methods whose options are rejected before credentials. For reports().list_goal_streams all three of skip/limit/search now fail with ErrorKind::Validation before auth (verified at crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:1572-1580), and search is rejected on list_attacks, get_prompt_sets, get_prompts_by_set, list_custom_attacks and get_error_logs. The behaviour break is fully documented in CHANGELOG.md:34-47 (satisfying the plan's per-parameter changelog requirement), but the primary API guide this phase was tasked with updating reads as if these fields are merely omitted when unset, so a consumer following RED_TEAM.md alone would be actively misled about a pre-transport rejection.
findings.required_fix: Reconcile the RED_TEAM.md pagination/request-constraints section with the current contract: state explicitly that the twelve listed option bindings now fail validation before credentials on their specific methods, and link the CHANGELOG migration table from that section rather than only from the "Current dataplane contract" preamble.

findings.description: The GNU evidence boundary still links checks/phase-08-ci-run-11/matrix-capture-receipt.json at source 72765d5 even though docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-12/matrix-capture-receipt.json is retained and newer. This is the still-open low follow-up recorded in docs/phase-status.json:1244-1251 ("Point docs/PLATFORMS.md at the newest retained GNU matrix receipt"), and PLATFORMS.md was edited in this phase (lines 30-37 add the vendor update boundary), so the stale pointer was carried forward in a document inside this phase's scope_evidence. It is not misleading about scope — line 16 names the source commit and lines 35-37 state that earlier GNU receipts do not establish fresh acceptance of this update — but the delivery document cites the older of two available receipts.
findings.required_fix: Point the GNU matrix receipt link at docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-12/matrix-capture-receipt.json with its actual source commit, or record in docs/phase-status.json why run-11 is deliberately retained as the cited receipt for this delivery.

findings.description: queryKinds is derived with `kinds[name] = branch.get("type", "string")`, accepting any OpenAPI type, but the runtime lowering in crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/common.rs:30-42 only handles "integer" and "boolean" explicitly and falls through to Value::String for everything else. The current pin declares only integer/string/boolean query kinds (confirmed: contract.json contains no "number", "array" or "object"), so there is no live defect, and a future "number" parameter would fail closed with a Validation error rather than reaching the wire wrongly typed. However this contradicts the plan's generation policy of failing on unsupported keywords/shapes instead of silently degrading, and the failure mode would surface as an unexplained caller-side validation error on a declared, legal parameter.
findings.required_fix: Assert in tools/red_team_dataplane.py that every derived queryKinds value is in the reviewed set {integer, boolean, string} and raise on anything else, so an unsupported query kind stops generation and requires a recorded classification instead of degrading to string coercion at runtime.

findings.description: Only the wire test name is machine-pinned (WIRE_TEST_NAME, enforced by wire_bindings at line 563-566). The new adversarial client-boundary tests that docs/VALIDATION.md:114-116 and docs/RED_TEAM.md:49 rely on for their claims — every_new_typed_vendor_route_rejects_contract_invalid_json_responses_after_dispatch, every_new_vendor_route_rechecks_destination_policy_before_authentication, six_new_vendor_writes_never_replay_transport_http_decode_or_limit_failures, csv_download_preserves_empty_non_utf8_and_exact_limit_bytes and the override/runtime-profile validators — are not referenced by any ledger, fixture binding or Python verifier. They are present and passed in this gate, but silently deleting one would not fail any coverage checker, unlike the removal of a native method or wire fixture.
findings.required_fix: Bind the new per-route negative tests by name in the vendor ledger's fixtureBinding (or an adjacent reviewed list checked by tools/red_team_dataplane.py / tools/test_red_team_dataplane.py), so the documented client-boundary security coverage cannot regress without failing a check.
